t.1.28.1: Then, as that immeasurable one asked about that forest, Viśvāmitra of great splendor began to explain it.
t.1.28.2: This, O Rāma, is the former hermitage of the great-souled Vāmana. It is renowned as Siddhāśrama, for here the great ascetic attained perfection.
t.1.28.3: At this very time, Bali, the king and son of Virocana, renowned in the three worlds, having conquered the hosts of gods together with Indra and together with the hosts of Maruts, held sway over that kingdom.
t.1.28.4: While Bali was performing his sacrifice, the gods, with Agni at their head, assembled and themselves spoke to Viṣṇu here in this hermitage.
t.1.28.5: O Viṣṇu, Bali, son of Virocana, is performing a supreme sacrifice; while that rite is not yet completed, let your own purpose be accomplished.
t.1.28.6: And whatever suppliants approach him from here and there, to them he gives everything, whatever is wanted, wherever and in the proper manner.
t.1.28.7: O Viṣṇu, you, for the sake of the welfare of the gods, have resorted to the power of māyā and assumed the state of a dwarf; accomplish the highest good.
t.1.28.9: Then Viṣṇu, of great splendor, was born of Aditi; assuming the form of a dwarf, he approached Vairocani.
t.1.28.8: By your grace this place will be known as Siddhāśrama. Now that the work is accomplished, lord of the gods, rise from here, O blessed one.
t.1.28.11: Having restrained Bali by his might, he gave the three worlds back to the great Indra; that one of great splendour again brought the three worlds under the sway of Śakra.
t.1.28.10: Then, having begged for three strides and received them with due honor, he who is the Self of the worlds, devoted to the welfare of all beings, strode across the worlds.
t.1.28.12: This hermitage, which dispels weariness, was formerly occupied by him; out of devotion to that Vāmana, it is now enjoyed by me as well.
t.1.28.13: To this hermitage come the rākṣasas who cause obstructions; here, O tiger among men, these evil-doers are to be slain by you.
t.1.28.14: Today, Rāma, we shall go to the unsurpassed Siddhāśrama. That hermitage, dear child, is yours just as it is mine.
t.1.28.15: Seeing him, all the sages dwelling in the Siddhāśrama sprang up again and again in haste and honored Viśvāmitra.
t.1.28.16: They offered due worship to the wise Viśvāmitra, and in the same way they performed the rites of hospitality for the two princes.
t.1.28.17: Then, having rested for a moment, the two princes, subduers of foes, the delights of the Raghus, with joined palms addressed the tiger among sages.
t.1.28.18: Enter upon your consecration this very day, O best of sages, and good fortune be with you! May this Siddhāśrama be truly accomplished, and may your word prove true.
t.1.28.19: Thus addressed, the greatly radiant Viśvāmitra, the great sage, then entered upon the consecration for the sacrifice, self-restrained and with his senses held in check.
t.1.28.20: The two princes, too, having spent that night with minds well composed, rose at daybreak and paid homage to Viśvāmitra.
